say.en: Bring a tiny test charge anywhere near a charged ball and it feels a push, without any contact. We describe that push per coulomb, at every point, as the electric field. In this lesson: Define electric field and find it for a point charge.
Draw and read electric field lines.

body.en: The *electric field* at a point is the force per unit positive test charge placed there: $\vec E = \vec F/q_0$. Its SI unit is N C⁻¹ (the same as V m⁻¹). For a point charge Q the field points away from a positive charge and towards a negative one, with magnitude $kQ/r^2$. A charge q placed in a field feels $\vec F = q\vec E$. The field of several charges is the vector sum of their fields.
body.kn: ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ಎಂದರೆ ಏಕಮಾನ ಧನ ಪರೀಕ್ಷಾ ಆವೇಶದ ಮೇಲಿನ ಬಲ; ಏಕಮಾನ N C⁻¹. ಬಿಂದು ಆವೇಶಕ್ಕೆ E = kQ/r². ಧನ ಆವೇಶದಿಂದ ಹೊರಕ್ಕೆ, ಋಣ ಆವೇಶದತ್ತ ಒಳಕ್ಕೆ. ಆವೇಶ q ಮೇಲಿನ ಬಲ F = qE.

points.en: Force on q: F = qE (opposite to E for negative q)

title.en: On the board: field of a point charge

narration.en: Put a tiny test charge q₀ near a charge Q: the force on it per coulomb is the electric field E. For a point charge E is kQ over r squared: away from a positive charge, towards a negative one. The field falls off as one over r squared, so it weakens quickly with distance. Field lines start on positive charges and end on negative charges. Two lines never cross and never close into loops; crowded lines mean a strong field.

body.en: A field line is a curve whose tangent at every point gives the direction of the field there. Lines start on positive charges and end on negative charges (or go to infinity). Two lines never cross, since the field has only one direction at a point. Electrostatic *field lines* never form closed loops. Where lines are crowded the field is strong; where they spread out it is weak.
body.kn: ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ರೇಖೆಗಳು ಧನ ಆವೇಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಆರಂಭವಾಗಿ ಋಣ ಆವೇಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೊನೆಗೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತವೆ. ಅವು ಎಂದಿಗೂ ಛೇದಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ ಮತ್ತು ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಕುಣಿಕೆಗಳನ್ನು ರೂಪಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ದಟ್ಟವಾದ ರೇಖೆಗಳು ಪ್ರಬಲ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರವನ್ನು ಸೂಚಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

heading.en: Electric Field, Field Lines and the Dipole

tagline.en: Electric field of a point charge and of a system of charges, field lines, continuous charge distributions, the electric dipole, its field on the axis and the equatorial line, and a dipole in a uniform field.

myth.en: A field line is the path along which a free positive charge will move.

truth.en: The tangent to a field line gives the direction of the force (and so of the acceleration), not of the velocity. A charge follows a field line only if the line is straight and the charge starts from rest. In a curved field a moving charge has inertia, so its path bends less sharply than the field line, just as a stone swung on a string flies off along a tangent.

say.en: A field line is a curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the field there. Lines start on positive charges and end on negative charges (or go to or come from infinity for a single charge).
An electric dipole is a pair of equal and opposite charges $+q$ and $-q$ separated by a small distance $2a$. Its dipole moment is $\vec p = q \times 2a$, pointing from $-q$ to $+q$ along the axis.

goal.en: Electric field of a point charge and of a system of charges, field lines, continuous charge distributions, the electric dipole, its field on the axis and the equatorial line, and a dipole in a uniform field.

question.en: At a point on the equatorial line of a short dipole, the electric field is:

explain.en: The components along the equatorial line cancel; what remains is parallel to the axis and points from +q towards −q, i.e. opposite to p.

task.en: Match each quantity with its SI unit.

explain.en: Each unit follows from its definition: E = F/q, p = q × 2a, λ = q/l, σ = q/S and τ = pE sin θ.

problem.en: An electron is placed in a uniform field of 2 × 10⁴ N C⁻¹. Find the force on it and its acceleration (mₑ = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg).

steps.en: F = eE = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ × 2 × 10⁴ = 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ N, opposite to E.

answer.en: 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ N opposite to E; about 3.5 × 10¹⁵ m s⁻²

narration.en: Let us solve this together. An electron is placed in a uniform field of 2 × 10⁴ N C⁻¹. Find the force on it and its acceleration (mₑ = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg).

say.en: Let us solve this together. An electron is placed in a uniform field of 2 times 10 to the power 4 newtons C to the power minus 1. Find the force on it and its acceleration (m e equals 9.1 times 10 to the power minus 31 kilograms).
F equals eE equals 1.6 times 10 to the power minus 19 times 2 times 10 to the power 4 equals 3.2 times 10 to the power minus 15 newtons, opposite to E.
a equals F over m equals 3.2 times 10 to the power minus 15 divided by 9.1 times 10 to the power minus 31.
a is approximately 3.5 times 10 to the power 15 metres s to the power minus 2.
So the answer is 3.2 times 10 to the power minus 15 newtons opposite to E; about 3.5 times 10 to the power 15 metres s to the power minus 2.

say.en: Pause and solve this exam pattern question. Charges plus 4 micro C and minus 4 micro C are 20 centimetres apart. The electric field at the midpoint is.
Each charge gives 9 times 10 to the power 9 times 4 times 10 to the power minus 6 over 0.1 squared equals 3.6 times 10 to the power 6 newtons C to the power minus 1.
Both fields point towards the negative charge, so they add: 7.2 times 10 to the power 6 newtons C to the power minus 1.

points.kn: ಬಿಂದು ಆವೇಶ: E = kQ/r², ಧನದಿಂದ ಹೊರಕ್ಕೆ, ಋಣದತ್ತ ಒಳಕ್ಕೆ.

narration.en: Recap. E = F/q₀; unit N C⁻¹. Point charge: E = kQ/r², away from + and towards −. Fields of many charges add as vectors. Field lines go from + to −, never cross, never close.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. E = F/q₀; ಏಕಮಾನ N C⁻¹. ಬಿಂದು ಆವೇಶ: E = kQ/r², ಧನದಿಂದ ಹೊರಕ್ಕೆ, ಋಣದತ್ತ ಒಳಕ್ಕೆ. ಅನೇಕ ಆವೇಶಗಳ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರಗಳು ಸದಿಶವಾಗಿ ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ರೇಖೆಗಳು ಧನದಿಂದ ಋಣಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತವೆ, ಛೇದಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ, ಮುಚ್ಚಿಕೊಳ್ಳುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. E equals F over q 0; unit N C to the power minus 1.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. E equals F over q 0; ಏಕಮಾನ N C to the power minus 1.

say.en: Fields of many charges add as vectors.

say.kn: ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ರೇಖೆಗಳು ಧನದಿಂದ ಋಣಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತವೆ, ಛೇದಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ, ಮುಚ್ಚಿಕೊಳ್ಳುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.
